title: Merge Sort
problemStatement: Sort an array using Merge Sort.
intuition: Divide into halves, sort each, merge two sorted runs. Merge needs O(n) temporary space. Guarantees O(n log n) — no TLE from quadratic worst case.

approaches.title: Merge sort
approaches.idea: Recurse left/right; merge with two pointers into temp, copy back.
approaches.spaceNote: Aux arrays O(n); recursion depth O(log n)
limitations: Extra O(n) memory — MLE risk if memory tight vs in-place quicksort
approaches.whyWorks: Merge of two sorted lists is sorted; induction on divide-and-conquer tree.

specialTechnique.title: Stable O(n log n) guarantee
specialTechnique.body: Use <= in merge to keep stability. Prefer merge sort when you need stable sort or hard O(n log n) worst case (vs quicksort’s average).

interviewInsight: Contrast with quicksort: merge = stable + worst O(n log n) + O(n) memory.
